correctness.rationale: For any connected spanning bipartite cactus H on N=p+q vertices with c cycles, the block-cut tree gives p≥c+1, q≥c+1, N≥3c+1 and |E(H)|=N−1+c. For k the minimum of these three bounds, take a base square, x=max(0,2k−p) additional squares attached at its first-part vertex, and k−1−x squares at its second-part vertex. Bounds 0≤x≤k−1 and x≤q−k−1 guarantee all vertex capacities. Add unused vertices as leaves. This attains N−1+k edges for all p,q≥1. Exhaustive direct cactus checks of 129226 labelled edge subsets across 20 inputs and constructive checks for 900 pairs corroborated the proof.

value.rationale: The exact unweighted cactus edge-deletion optimum on every K_{p,q} is a natural parameterized dense-family benchmark for a problem hard even on bipartite graphs. Three structurally distinct sharp bottlenecks and an O(p+q)-size optimal witness are a substantive all-family result, not a restatement of the published N-vertex bound or isolated numeric optimization.
